steps: Shared heights give area ABD : area ADC = 3:1; E halves AC, so area ABD : area ADE = 6:1.
ABD and ADE share base AD. Comparing their heights, then the similar right triangles along BE, gives BP:PE = 6:1.
Let the whole triangle's height above BC be h. E is at height h/2, so P is at (6/7)(h/2) = 3h/7.
The distance from A down to the parallel through P is therefore h − 3h/7 = 4h/7.
The triangle above that lower parallel is similar to ABC. Its area is (4/7)² × 588 = 192 cm².
The triangle above the parallel through E has half the linear scale of ABC, so its area is 588/4 = 147 cm².
The shaded strip is the larger of those two nested triangles minus the smaller. Subtract their areas, not their linear scale factors.
